plants.name: Bamboo palm (Chamaedorea seifrizii)
plants.tip: Prone to fungal leaf spotting in stagnant air. Give it room to breathe and let the surface dry between waterings.
plants.colour: Mid-green short leaflets on thin clustering canes

plants.name: Cat palm (Chamaedorea cataractarum)
plants.tip: It grows beside streams and will not forgive a dry rootball. Tips brown first, and those fronds stay brown.
plants.colour: Glossy deep green, dense arching clump with no visible trunk

plants.name: Metallic palm (Chamaedorea metallica)
plants.tip: One of the few palms that genuinely copes with a dim corner, and it shrugs off spider mite better than most.
plants.colour: Blue-green undivided leaves with a metallic sheen, split at the tip

plants.name: Chamaedorea radicalis
plants.tip: The trunkless form takes more sun and more cold than any other Chamaedorea. Flower spikes rise above the leaves.
plants.colour: Stiff dark green pinnate leaves from a trunkless base, red fruit on females

plants.name: Chamaedorea radicalis (trunking form)
plants.tip: The same tolerance as the trunkless form, but it keeps climbing. Give it head height before you commit to a spot.
plants.colour: Narrower green leaflets on a slim ringed trunk

plants.name: Hardy bamboo palm (Chamaedorea microspadix)
plants.tip: The clump leans outwards as the canes age. Cut the oldest out at the base rather than shortening them.
plants.colour: Small green leaflets with a grey cast beneath, on very thin canes

plants.name: Chamaedorea hooperiana
plants.tip: A better indoor reed palm than seifrizii: faster, fuller, and far less prone to fungal spotting.
plants.colour: Long arching mid-green pinnate leaves on inch-thick clustering canes

plants.name: Baby queen palm (Chamaedorea plumosa)
plants.tip: Quick growing, and it wants more light than the shade Chamaedoreas. In a dim room it stretches and thins.
plants.colour: Soft plumose bright green leaves on a single slim trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea glaucifolia
plants.tip: The white bloom on the stems rubs off and does not come back, so handle it by the pot rather than the trunk.
plants.colour: Grass-fine grey-green plumose leaves, waxy white bloom on the stems

plants.name: Whale tail palm (Chamaedorea ernesti-augusti)
plants.tip: Direct sun scorches the broad leaf within days. Shade and steady moisture keep it unmarked.
plants.colour: A single broad glossy green leaf split into two lobes at the tip

plants.name: Chamaedorea geonomiformis
plants.tip: A twenty-year-old plant is still under a metre. Do not repot to force growth; it only sulks.
plants.colour: Small undivided dark green leaves with pointed split tips

plants.name: Chamaedorea adscendens
plants.tip: Under a metre, and slow with it. Plant three or four to a pot, which is how it is meant to look.
plants.colour: Blue-green iridescent leaves on thin white-tan stems

plants.name: Chamaedorea amabilis
plants.tip: It tolerates neither a cold windowsill nor dry air. Warm, humid and shaded, or it declines steadily.
plants.colour: Thin undivided bright green leaves, split and toothed at the tip

plants.name: Chamaedorea arenbergiana
plants.tip: The leaves reach a metre and a half across, so it needs floor space rather than a shelf.
plants.colour: Broad dark green leaflets with long drip tips, on a dark green ringed trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea benziei
plants.tip: Among the easiest of the genus, and it takes more sun than most. Use a wide pot for the upright leaves.
plants.colour: Upright dark green pinnate leaves on a short ringed trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea brachypoda
plants.tip: Hard tap water browns the leaf tips. Rainwater or filtered water keeps them clean.
plants.colour: Dark green undivided leaves, sometimes mottled in lighter green

plants.name: Chamaedorea costaricana
plants.tip: It reaches four metres outdoors, so indoors expect to take whole canes out at the base each year.
plants.colour: Full mid-green pinnate leaves on clustering inch-thick canes

plants.name: Chamaedorea deckeriana
plants.tip: Salts in tap water show as brown tips on the thin leaves. Flush the pot through with clean water monthly.
plants.colour: Thin undivided deep green leaf, split at the tip

plants.name: Chamaedorea fragrans
plants.tip: Nearly every plant in cultivation is a male clone raised from cuttings, so do not wait for seed.
plants.colour: Small pointed undivided green leaves on very thin reed-like canes

plants.name: Chamaedorea klotzschiana
plants.tip: The grouped leaflets are the whole point of it, so stand it where you see the leaf side on.
plants.colour: Green leaflets grouped along the rachis at odd angles, like rows of bow ties

plants.name: Chamaedorea linearis
plants.tip: Over six metres in time, so it belongs in a conservatory rather than a room.
plants.colour: Long green leaves above a pale-ringed trunk, crownshaft mottled green and yellow

plants.name: Chamaedorea nationsiana
plants.tip: Shade, even moisture and no cold draughts. It is scarce enough that a lost plant is hard to replace.
plants.colour: Wide green leaflets with pronounced drip tips on a thin trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea neurochlamys
plants.tip: A reliable grower for the genus. Keep it above freezing and out of direct sun and it asks for little.
plants.colour: Wide puffy green leaflets with drip tips, a white collar at the leaf base when young

plants.name: Chamaedorea sartorii
plants.tip: Easily confused with oblongata and neurochlamys. Check for the orange flower bracts before you buy.
plants.colour: Slim green pinnate leaves, orange flower bracts and black seeds

plants.name: Chamaedorea schiedeana
plants.tip: The trunk stays pencil-thin as it climbs to four metres. Stake it, or grow several in one pot.
plants.colour: Wide puffy green leaflets on a very thin dark green trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea stolonifera
plants.tip: It spreads by rooting runners. Detach one that has rooted and leafed out and you have a second plant.
plants.colour: Small undivided green leaves with blunt tips, spreading on runners

plants.name: Chamaedorea sullivaniorum
plants.tip: Under half a metre, and it wants warmth and shade throughout. One night below freezing will kill it.
plants.colour: Thick pleated leaves, green to silvery blue-green, sometimes mottled

plants.name: Pacaya palm (Chamaedorea tepejilote)
plants.tip: Direct sunlight burns it, and it needs real head height. Deep shade and a tall room, or leave it outside.
plants.colour: Long dark green leaves with S-curved leaflets, trunk dark green with white rings

plants.name: Potato chip palm (Chamaedorea tuerckheimii)
plants.tip: A terrarium palm rather than a room palm. It stays under half a metre and wants constant humidity.
plants.colour: Tiny rippled undivided leaves, green or silver-frosted blue-green

plants.name: Chamaedorea warscewiczii
plants.tip: Filtered light and steady moisture. The crownshaft is barely there, which sets it apart from its relatives.
plants.colour: Short irregular green leaves, the end leaflets wider than the rest

plants.name: Chamaedorea woodsoniana
plants.tip: The largest of the genus, well over ten metres. It wants sun and plenty of water, not a living room.
plants.colour: Deep green keeled leaves on a thick trunk with a clear crownshaft

plants.name: Chamaedorea oblongata
plants.tip: Takes deeper shade than most reed palms, but not a soggy pot. Drain it hard and water less than you think.
plants.colour: Broad dark green leaflets with drip tips on a single slim ringed trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea tenella
plants.tip: Small enough for a terrarium and it needs the humidity of one. Dry room air stops it dead.
plants.colour: Small undivided leaves, dark green above with a purple flush beneath

plants.name: Chamaedorea pochutlensis
plants.tip: Takes more sun and drought than the shade species, but the clump crowds fast. Thin old canes at the base.
plants.colour: Stiff grey-green pinnate leaves on stout clustering canes

plants.name: Chamaedorea elatior
plants.tip: It climbs by hooked leaflet tips and will grab whatever is nearest. Give it a support before it finds one.
plants.colour: Long green leaves with hooked reflexed tips on scrambling stems

plants.name: Chamaedorea pinnatifrons
plants.tip: The most variable species in the genus, but every form wants the same thing: shade, warmth, even moisture.
plants.colour: Slim green pinnate leaves on a thin solitary ringed trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea seleriana
plants.tip: The thick leaves hold water, so it rots long before it wilts. Wait until the top third of the pot is dry.
plants.colour: Thick leathery leaves, deep green with a matt velvety surface

plants.name: Chamaedorea graminifolia
plants.tip: The fine leaflets shred in moving air, so keep it clear of doorways and fan-assisted heating.
plants.colour: Very narrow grass-like green leaflets on tall clustering canes

plants.name: Chamaedorea pumila
plants.tip: It stays under thirty centimetres for life. Treat it as a terrarium plant rather than a pot plant.
plants.colour: Tiny undivided leaves, dark green mottled with silver

plants.name: Chamaedorea rhizomatosa
plants.tip: It creeps sideways on rhizomes rather than clumping upwards, so give it a wide shallow pot.
plants.colour: Small pinnate green leaves rising singly from a creeping rhizome

plants.name: Chamaedorea dammeriana
plants.tip: A small understorey palm that wants warmth all year. A cold snap blackens the growing point first.
plants.colour: Thin dark green leaves with few broad leaflets, split at the tip

plants.name: Chamaedorea allenii
plants.tip: Constant shade and constant warmth. It marks permanently if a shaft of afternoon sun reaches it.
plants.colour: Broad dark green leaflets with long drip tips on a thin trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea alternans
plants.tip: Slow and steady in deep shade. Feed at half strength, because a full dose burns the leaflet tips.
plants.colour: Green leaflets set alternately along an arching rachis

plants.name: Chamaedorea falcifera
plants.tip: Shade, warmth and even moisture. The curved leaflets crease if you push it through a doorway.
plants.colour: Narrow sickle-curved green leaflets on a slender solitary trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea foveata
plants.tip: Deep shade and a coarse open compost. Fine peat holds too much water around its thin roots.
plants.colour: Dark green pinnate leaves on a slim green ringed trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea frondosa
plants.tip: It builds a wide crown, so measure the space first. Cut spent fronds flush to the trunk, not part way.
plants.colour: Full dark green pinnate leaves on a stout ringed trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea liebmannii
plants.tip: Drier and brighter than most of the genus suits it, but never let the pot dry out to the base.
plants.colour: Slim green leaflets held stiffly upright on a thin cane

plants.name: Chamaedorea macrospadix
plants.tip: One of the cooler-tolerant species. A shaded porch suits it better than a warm centrally heated room.
plants.colour: Dark green pinnate leaves on a solitary slim trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea nubium
plants.tip: A cloud-forest palm: cool, shaded and humid. Central heating dries it faster than it can recover.
plants.colour: Narrow green leaflets on thin clustering stems

plants.name: Chamaedorea oreophila
plants.tip: It comes from higher ground and takes a cool winter well. Cut watering back sharply once growth stops.
plants.colour: Stiff mid-green leaflets on a short trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea pygmaea
plants.tip: The stem sits below soil level, so plant it no deeper than it came and keep compost off the crown.
plants.colour: Very small stiff blue-green leaves from an underground stem

plants.name: Chamaedorea queroana
plants.tip: Shade, warmth and steady moisture. It drops its lower fronds quickly if the rootball ever dries out.
plants.colour: Broad green leaflets on a slender green trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea rigida
plants.tip: Stiff and sun-tolerant for the genus, so it will take a brighter window than most of its relatives.
plants.colour: Rigid upright grey-green leaves on a short thick stem

plants.name: Chamaedorea robertii
plants.tip: Deep shade suits it. An afternoon in direct sun bleaches the leaves and they never green up again.
plants.colour: Undivided to few-leafleted deep green leaves on thin stems

plants.name: Chamaedorea sciurea
plants.tip: Warm shade and constant moisture. It resents cold roots, so lift the pot off a stone floor in winter.
plants.colour: Soft mid-green pinnate leaves on a slim green trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea simplex
plants.tip: Slow, small and shade-loving. Repot only once roots circle the pot; disturbance sets it back a season.
plants.colour: Simple undivided green leaves split at the tip

plants.name: Chamaedorea stricta
plants.tip: One of the drier-growing species. Let the compost dry two thirds down before watering it again.
plants.colour: Stiff upright grey-green leaves on a short solitary stem

plants.name: Chamaedorea undulatifolia
plants.tip: The rippled leaf edge only develops in humid air. In a dry room the new leaves come out flat.
plants.colour: Undivided green leaves with a strongly undulating margin

plants.name: Chamaedorea velutina
plants.tip: The velvety leaf surface holds water spots, so water the compost and keep it off the foliage.
plants.colour: Deep green leaves with a soft velvety texture

plants.name: Chamaedorea whitelockiana
plants.tip: Shade and shelter. The long leaves tear along the ribs in moving air, and a torn frond stays torn.
plants.colour: Long arching dark green pinnate leaves on a slim trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea ibarrae
plants.tip: A small shade palm that wants warmth year round. Keep it above fifteen degrees and it grows steadily.
plants.colour: Broad undivided dark green leaves, deeply split at the tip

plants.name: Chamaedorea ehrenbergii
plants.tip: Shaded, humid and frost-free. It resents being moved about, so pick its spot and leave it there.
plants.colour: Undivided to bifid dark green leaves on thin stems

plants.name: Chamaedorea carchensis
plants.tip: A cool cloud-forest species. It does better on a shaded porch in summer than in a warm dry room.
plants.colour: Narrow dark green leaflets on a thin solitary stem

plants.name: Chamaedorea parvisecta
plants.tip: Dust settles in the fine leaflets and invites spider mite. Rinse the whole leaf under a tap monthly.
plants.colour: Many very narrow green leaflets on an arching leaf

plants.name: Chamaedorea vulgata
plants.tip: Among the more forgiving of the rarer species. Shade, warmth and an open compost are enough.
plants.colour: Mid-green pinnate leaves on a slender ringed trunk

plants.name: Chamaedorea brachyclada
plants.tip: Very short-stemmed and slow. Stand it low and close to eye level, where the leaf shape actually reads.
plants.colour: Broad undivided green leaves on a very short stem
